**Explanation (80 words):**

Your bishop on b3 is undefended and attacked twice—by the knight and the a2-pawn. Instead of defending or moving it, capture the bishop with Nxb3. Black's only way to fight back is Bxc5+, checking your king, but then your knight recaptures on c5. Now your knight forks the bishop and b7-pawn. When Black tries Re2+ for counterplay, you simply capture the rook with your king, winning the exchange. The lesson: a piece attacked twice but defended only once (or not at all) is vulnerable to capture. Always check if your opponent can ignore your threats and create their own.
